<thought>All three building blocks (5‑chloro‑1,2,4‑triazine, 4‑(azetidin‑1‑yl)‑benzyl bromide, and 4‑methoxy‑aniline) are commercially available and inexpensive. I will use two standard retrosynthetic transformations: (1) an SNAr substitution of the aryl chloride (template ID 1307732) to introduce the benzyl‑azetidine side chain, and (2) an amide‑formation (template ID 1001) to couple the remaining exocyclic amine of the triazine with 4‑methoxy‑aniline. The resulting retrosynthetic tree satisfies the ≤ 3‑step limit and stays under the $9 999 budget. 

Here is the required JSON representation of the route.

  "type": "mol",
  "smiles": "COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1",

      "template_id": 1001,
      "children": [

        },
        {

          "smiles": "C(c1ncnc(N)n1)Cc2ccc(CN3CC(F)C3)cc2"
        }
      ]
    },
    {

        }
      ]
    }

}
